A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Algorithms, proofs, and experiments can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy-model convergence experiments, RADD text-generation perplexities, MaskGIT image-generation FIDs, and parameter sensitivity studies in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds GSM8K reasoning results, additional sampler comparisons and text-quality measurements, and empirical intensity-positivity diagnostics.

M1.justification: The two principal solvers remain. V2 adds a current-state jump-validity indicator to RK-2 Algorithm 1, absent from both v1 Algorithm 1 and its practical Algorithm 4, and introduces a blockwise Trapezoidal variant in Appendix D.4. Positive-part clipping and the wider theta range already existed in v1 Appendix D.1.

E1.justification: V2 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning with LLaDA-Instruct, substantially extending task coverage beyond text and image generation. The RADD/OpenWebText, MaskGIT/ImageNet, and toy experiments remain. Renaming the toy experiment from 15-dimensional to 15-state does not introduce different data; v1 Appendix D.2 already specifies 15 states.

E2.justification: V2 adds FHS to the reported text and image comparisons and Semi-AR to RADD text generation. Its new GSM8K comparison evaluates confidence-based and random-remasking Semi-AR variants. FHS was discussed in v1 but was absent from these benchmark comparisons; existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds LLaMA 3 perplexity and unigram-entropy evaluation. The new GSM8K protocol uses an 8B model, zero-shot 256-token responses, 64–256 NFEs, temperature 0.5, and full-sequence versus blocksize-8 conditions. Existing toy, RADD, and MaskGIT sampling budgets are retained; these additions do not establish reruns of the original experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds positivity measurements across NFE budgets, directly probing a convergence-theory assumption (Table 6), and a blockwise versus full-sequence reasoning comparison probing generation order (Table 7). Existing convergence and theta-sensitivity studies remain; their relocation and renumbering do not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: V2 Table 6 newly reports plus/minus quantities alongside positivity percentages, but does not define their statistical meaning or associated repetition counts. The toy experiment retains 1,000 bootstrap resamples and 95% confidence intervals. An increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds baseline, LLaMA 3, entropy, positivity, and GSM8K results. On GSM8K, Trapezoidal scores 38.4% versus random Semi-AR's 34.3% at NFE 128, but 39.7% versus 40.3% at NFE 256. Shared GPT-2 perplexities remain unchanged in v2 Table 3; however, v2 Table 1 inconsistently reports RK-2 as 36.330 instead of 33.971 at NFE 1024.

T1.justification: V2 introduces periodic boundary conditions in Section 5.1 and an O(kappa) rejection argument in Remark C.4. Remark C.6 adds an expected-positivity derivation. Proposition C.20 revises v1 Proposition C.16's local error bound from O(Delta_n^3 epsilon_II + Delta_n^4) to O(Delta_n^3), with altered reasoning. The final second-order KL convergence rate is retained.

C1.justification: The central claims of introducing high-order discrete-diffusion solvers and establishing second-order KL convergence remain. The abstract broadens empirical applicability to GSM8K reasoning and claims gains across models ranging from 200M to 8B parameters, extending the practical contribution without redefining the main algorithmic contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies the unresolved positivity issue and explains periodicity versus rejection qualifications, extending v1's existing positivity discussion. It also interprets blockwise gains through LLaDA's preference for left-to-right generation and qualifies the reasoning advantage as primarily occurring at low NFE (Section 6.4 and Appendix D.4).

D1.justification: V2 adds a project code-repository link, identifies GPT-2 Large and LLaMA 3 evaluator checkpoints, and documents the LLaDA checkpoint, noise schedule, early stopping, temperature, block lengths, hardware, and evaluation harness. V1 already supplied RADD/MaskGIT checkpoint information and implementation settings; v2 substantially expands this reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands references and positioning toward diffusion-LLM reasoning, discrete neural sampling, and inference-time scaling, including LLaDA, Dream, and d1. Section 1.1 and Appendix A also add numerical CTMC and diffusion-solver literature. These are substantive literature additions beyond the switch to numbered citations.

P1.justification: V2 edits and condenses prose while retaining the basic narrative. It merges v1 Section 3.3 into Section 4, moves stochastic formulations into Appendix C.1, integrates the practical RK-2 presentation into Algorithm 1, and converts the hyperparameter section into a remark. Most existing exposition and proof text remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column format with wrapped algorithms and tables. Figure 1 gains a solver schematic, comparison plots gain FHS curves and legends, and tables are added or expanded. Existing sensitivity plots and the identical Figure 7 image samples are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens practical validation through previously missing sampler comparisons, additional text-quality and diversity measurements, and an 8B reasoning evaluation. Positivity diagnostics, more explicit theoretical conditions, and expanded code and implementation information improve assessability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the localized RK-2 table inconsistency and undefined plus/minus reporting. The empirical positivity checks nevertheless do not remove the theorem's positivity assumption.
